findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P), conditions of certification (if applicable) (P), and additional conditions (if applicable) (C).

The bottle of bleach solution used in the kitchen is observed to bleach out the inspector’s test strips. This indicates a concentration significantly to strong for safe use in a kitchen. Education took place and the bottle remade during this inspection to correct. When making a bottle of the size used in the kitchen approximately a teaspoon of bleach should be sufficient when filling the rest of the bottle with water. Use the available test strips to verify concentration each time a bottle is made.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

On arrival the PIC could not provide a verification method for the dish machine’s sanitize step. The issue was discussed and multiple options suggested. Due to the holidays and inspector vacations the follow-up is being pushed out to January 2nd of 2025.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

A bottle of Microban is observed to be used for spraying surfaces in the kitchen. At the time of the spraying a freshly cleaned rack of food contact utensils is observed in the immediate area being sprayed. The bottle of Microban indicates that it is intended for only no-food contact surfaces. A discussion took place and the bottle of bleach solution will be the only surface sanitizer used in the kitchen moving foreword. Ensure that any chemical used on food related surfaces is intended for food contact.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

1) The counter above the dish machine is warping and exposing the particle board underneath. Repair prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The junction between the dish sink and the wall is pulling away from each other. Seal the wall/counter junctions prior to the next routine inspection. Caulking suggested.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
No vomit/diarrhea clean up policy on file. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided clean up policy. Keep on file in case norovirus clean up is required.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Milk in the baby room fridge observed ~50F. CORRECTED-- Cooler temperature was adjusted and milk that was stored in the fridge overnight was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility needs to have an irreversible registering temperature indicator/thermometer to verify that the dish machine is reaching proper sanitizing temperature. An irreversible thermometer or single-use temperature indicating stickers/strips would be sufficient.
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Main employee responsible for food handling/prep in the kitchen has a food handler certification but has not yet completed the food manager course. Employee is registered to take a course through MJ Kellner next month. 
Provide proof of certification.

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee entered the kitchen and did not wash hands prior to putting away clean dishes. Handwashing was discussed, and employee washed hands prior to continuing with the task. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival kitchen handsink was blocked with gallon milk jugs. Jugs were removed from the sink and discarded. Proper use of handsink was discussed.

Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Can opener blade was soiled with food buildup from previous use. Can opener was last used on Friday and had not yet been used to open cans today. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized prior to use.

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses or up to every 4hrs after continuous use for items such as the can opener and other in-use equipment.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was observed at 80°F at ambient temperature. Staff noted the thermometer had not been calibrated since it was purchased. Ice water method was used to check the thermometer, which was reading around 40°F. Pliers were used to properly calibrate the thermometer to 32°F in the ice water solution. 

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions used on general surfaces in the kitchen. Some test strips were provided by inspector. Staff were advised to purchase strips for checking the quat sanitizer. (see general comments for additional information)

 A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.
